messages:
ben: Hey team — customer hitting intermittent 401s then 429s when prefetching large contexts (64k). Started after they switched to parallel prefetch of ~24 requests. Logs: '401 Unauthorized' for some requests, then quick 429s. Can we triage?
neha: Thanks @ben — can you paste a minimal repro + curl and any response headers (x-rwd-*)?
ben: Curl snippet: ```curl -v -H \"Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY\" -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" -d '{"model":"rwd-64k-latest","input":"<long doc>","stream":true}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate``` Response headers seen sometimes: `x-rwd-rpm-limit: 600`, `x-rwd-tpm-limit: 180000`, `x-rwd-current-rpm: 598`, `x-rwd-current-tpm: 177500` and occasionally `x-rwd-reason: concurrency_exceeded`.
neha: Good, that helps. Two quick checks: 1) Are they rotating API keys frequently from their side? 401s could be intermittent auth failures. 2) Are they fanouting the same long context to many model calls in parallel (prefetch)?
sam: Poked infra metrics for model `rwd-64k-latest` around that time window. Saw per-model concurrent handlers spike to ~220 (limit configured for hosted tier is 200), and token rate hit ~98% of RPM window for a few mins. Queue length also increased. Ops alert fired: ops-bot: "ALERT: per-model queue >500 for rwd-64k-latest at 2026-03-04T15:24:xxZ"
maria: Likely combo: (a) their client does aggressive parallel prefetch (24) AND (b) long-context requests cost many tokens so TMP gets exhausted quickly -> auth 401s are probably client-side rotates or slightly malformed tokens on retry that then trigger 401, which leads to immediate retry and then 429s when they resume.
neha: For repro, ask customer to run two variants: 1) single-client linear requests (no prefetch), 2) same load but with concurrency limited to 6. Also capture full response headers and any trace IDs.
ben: They shared trace ids: trace: td-6a1b, td-6a1c, td-6a1d. Attaching snippets: one 401 response body: `\{"error\":{\"message\":\"Invalid API key\",\"type\":\"auth_error\"}}` then later a 429 with `\{"error\":{\"message\":\"Rate limit exceeded - model per-minute quota\"}}`.
sam: From backend traces those trace ids show: a handful of failed auth checks (token expired) around client-side rotation times, then a fanout spike that saturated the per-model concurrency headroom -> requests were queued and eventually rejected with 429.
maria: Immediate mitigation suggestions to pass to the customer: 1) Reduce prefetch parallelism to <=8 for rwd-64k-latest. 2) Add exponential backoff for 429s with jitter. 3) Prefer streaming or chunked requests to avoid full 64k inflight per request when possible. 4) If they need sustained high throughput, consider Dedicated capacity or reserving more throughput for that model variant.
neha: I'll post a tiny retry snippet for them.
maria: Nice — keep it short.
neha: ```python
# simple backoff pseudocode
import time, random
def call_with_retries(fn, max_retries=6):
    for i in range(max_retries):
        resp = fn()
        if resp.status_code == 200:
            return resp
        if resp.status_code == 401:
            # surface to app, do not retry blindly
            raise Exception('auth error')
        if resp.status_code == 429:
            sleep = (2 ** i) * 0.1 + random.random()*0.1
            time.sleep(sleep)
            continue
    raise Exception('max retries')
```
sam: Also recommend they log `x-rwd-current-rpm`, `x-rwd-current-tpm`, and `x-rwd-concurrency` on every response so they can see approaching limits rather than hit them.
ben: Customer wants a clear rule-of-thumb: concurrency limits per model and how context length affects it. Can we provide a short explainer?
maria: Rule-of-thumb: 1) Per-model concurrency limit is enforced as handlers (roughly 200 for hosted rwd-64k-latest in this tenant) — concurrent streaming sessions count fully. 2) Longer contexts increase TPM/RPM usage because each request consumes tokens for prompt + expected completion; many long contexts -> TMP exhaustion sooner. 3) Fanout/prefetch multiplies concurrency and token TPS. 4) If you need both low latency and high throughput with large contexts, prefer Dedicated capacity or reduce per-request context length (chunking + prefix cache).
neha: I'll summarize for the customer and ask them to try the two repro variants. If they still see 401s, we escalate to security to inspect key rotation.
ben: I'll send this to them now. Thanks. :thumbsup: 
ops-bot: "NOTE: Consider recommending reserved capacity if customer traffic is sustained and critical — see docs/setup/dedicated"
ben: Confirmed customer will throttle prefetch to 6 and test backoff. Will update thread with results later. Thanks everyone.
